questions.q: Why does the Facilities Request table need both a UI Policy and a Data Policy for the destination-location requirement?
options: A UI Policy makes the form usable when filled out directly; a Data Policy enforces the same rule server-side so it holds even if a record bypasses the form entirely
Data Policies are a newer replacement for UI Policies and both should never be used together
UI Policies and Data Policies do exactly the same thing, so using both is redundant
Only a Data Policy is actually necessary; the UI Policy adds nothing
questions.explain: Lesson 22's framing is repeated here: the UI Policy handles form behavior, the Data Policy is the backstop that holds regardless of how the record is created.

questions.q: What might cause a correctly configured notification to never actually send, per the System Properties check in this lesson?
options: The notification record was deleted
Outbound email being disabled at the instance level, even though the notification itself is configured correctly
The catalog item has no variable set
The requester's role was never created
questions.explain: Lesson 25's System Properties lesson is exactly where an admin discovers outbound email is off instance-wide, silently defeating an otherwise correct notification.

questions.q: What does an Update Set NOT capture, according to this lesson?
options: Catalog items and their variable sets
ACLs and UI/Data Policies
User records and group memberships
Notification records and email templates
questions.explain: Lesson 29 established that Update Sets capture configuration, not user accounts or group membership, which must exist independently in each environment.

questions.q: Per this lesson's recommended path, who should test a completed Update Set in the Test instance before it moves to Production?
options: Nobody — testing in Dev alone is sufficient
Only the administrator who built it
Someone other than the builder, ideally an actual end user like a Lakeview coordinator
The Production instance's own users, after the set is already committed there
questions.explain: The lesson calls for a second person — ideally a real coordinator — to walk through the actual workflow in Test before anything touches Production.

questions.q: According to the administration checklist, what should happen if a problem is found after an Update Set has already moved to Production?
options: Hand-patch the issue directly in Production to save time
Ignore it unless a user complains
Fix it in Dev, re-test, and move a corrected Update Set through Dev to Test to Production again
Delete the entire Update Set and start over with no testing
questions.explain: The checklist and Lesson 32's common-problems guidance both call for fixing issues upstream and re-running the same promotion path, never patching Production directly.
